title: Shell Regulation of Sustained-Release Microcapsules for Oilfield Profile Control and Flooding
content: In oilfield chemical flooding, chemical agents such as surfactants and polymers are susceptible to loss through adsorption, retention, and degradation, which can limit their effectiveness in deep-reservoir profile control and flooding. Sustained-release microcapsules provide an emerging approach for the deep delivery of chemical agents by encapsulating and protecting them within a shell to achieve controlled release. In this review, the microcapsule shell is considered a key functional interface linking chemical-agent protection, reservoir transport, and deep release. Focusing on shell composition, structural regulation, and stimuli-responsive properties, the effects of shell thickness, porosity, crosslinking density, and multilayer structures on microcapsule stability and release behavior are systematically analyzed. Different release mechanisms are summarized, and the effects of shell design on the controlled release and deep-reservoir performance of typical oilfield chemical agents, including surfactants, polymers, gels, and gel breakers, are discussed. In response to the challenges of insufficient stability under high-temperature and high-salinity conditions and the difficulty in coordinating transport with release, future research directions are proposed, including multiscale shell structural design, synergistic responses to multiple stimuli, and coupled transport–release mechanisms, with the aim of enabling precise controlled release and reservoir-adaptive design.
